mechanism_narrative: Rising housing starts (HOUST) indicate strong consumer demand for new homes, which typically signals robust economic growth and positive equity market sentiment, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 5-day returns in more than 60% of periods when HOUST is rising (measured by 3-month rolling growth > 0.5%) over a 5-year walk-forward window.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate exceeds 4.5%, it signals a tightening monetary policy that increases discount rates for equities, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 20-day returns in more than 60% of periods when FEDFUNDS > 4.5% over a 5-year walk-forward window.

mechanism_narrative: A strong labor market, indicated by both rising employment (PAYEMS growth > 0.3% monthly) and low unemployment (UNRATE < 4.5%), signals robust consumer spending and corporate earnings, driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: The joint signal of PAYEMS growth > 0.3% and UNRATE < 4.5% fails to produce positive 20-day returns in more than 60% of instances over a 5-year walk-forward window.

mechanism_narrative: In monetary tightening cycles, elevated inflation (CPIAUCSL) and rising interest rates (FEDFUNDS) compress equity valuations, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 60-day returns in more than 60% of periods classified as monetary tightening cycles (CPIAUCSL > 2.0% YoY and FEDFUNDS > 4.0%) over a 5-year walk-forward window.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in industrial production (INDPRO) below 105.0 indicates weakening manufacturing activity, which typically precedes negative equity market returns, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 5-day returns in more than 60% of periods when INDPRO < 105.0 over a 5-year walk-forward window.

mechanism_narrative: Rising inflation (CPIAUCSL) signals increasing price pressures that prompt central bank tightening, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 20-day returns in more than 60% of periods when CPIAUCSL is rising (3-month YoY growth > 2.0%) over a 5-year walk-forward window.

mechanism_narrative: When both inflation (CPIAUCSL) and the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) are rising, it indicates a dual threat of high inflation and monetary tightening, which compresses equity valuations and causes negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: The joint signal of CPIAUCSL growth > 1.0% and FEDFUNDS growth > 0.25% fails to produce negative 20-day returns in more than 60% of instances over a 5-year walk-forward window.

mechanism_narrative: In late-cycle expansions, strong GDP growth (GDPC1) signals that the economy is approaching its peak, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days as investors anticipate a slowdown.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 60-day returns in more than 60% of periods classified as late-cycle expansion (GDPC1 growth > 3.0% YoY) over a 5-year walk-forward window.
